title: Are all angles of symmetry multiples of the smallest?
description: The lists of angles of symmetry for two, three and four angles are compared. Each list is the smallest angle added again and again up to the full turn. Keeko's doubt is that a figure may fit at an angle in between.
teaching_notes: One idea: turning by the smallest angle again and again gives every angle of symmetry, so each one is a multiple of the smallest. Watch for students who think an angle in between could also fit.

source: Angles of symmetry when there are exactly 2 of them: 180°, 3
video_script.why: The child sees that the angles of symmetry are the smallest angle added again and again, so each one is a multiple of it.
video_script.substitution: the book's lists of angles for two, three and four angles of symmetry, each written as the smallest angle repeated
video_script.anchor: the book's three lists of angles of symmetry, for two, three and four angles
video_script.wrong_answer: a figure may fit at an angle in between
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says a figure with smallest angle ninety degrees may also fit at one hundred degrees.
video_script.payoff_line: The angles of symmetry are always multiples of the smallest angle

final_answer.value: Yes, the angles of symmetry are always multiples of the smallest angle of symmetry
final_answer.spoken: yes, the angles of symmetry are always multiples of the smallest angle of symmetry

hold_back: Yes, the angles of symmetry are always multiples of the smallest angle
maths_rules: turning by the smallest angle again and again fits each time, so every multiple fits
if a figure with smallest angle 90° also fitted at 100°, turning back by 90° would make it fit at 10°, which is smaller than the smallest angle; this cannot be
video_script.design: The three lists from the book, each rewritten as the smallest angle repeated. Then a figure with smallest angle seventy two degrees is turned again and again. Keeko's doubt is that an angle in between could fit.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, about angles of symmetry.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two angles are one hundred eighty and three hundred sixty degrees.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Three angles are one hundred twenty, two hundred forty and three hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four angles are ninety, one hundred eighty, two hundred seventy and three hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>In each list, the angles are multiples of the smallest angle.
Will this always happen?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a figure with a dot at its centre; a curved arrow round the dot; the words angle of symmetry: a turn after which the figure looks the same

marks.dot: the dot at the centre lights up
marks.name: the curved arrow and the words angle of symmetry appear

narration: <bookmark mark='dot'/>The figure turns about the dot at its centre.
<bookmark mark='name'/>A turn after which it looks exactly the same is an angle of symmetry.

beats.on_screen: Given: the angles of symmetry for exactly 2, 3 and 4 angles, each ending at 360°
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the three lists of angles of symmetry from your book.
Each list ends at the full turn.

beats.on_screen: To find: will the angles always be multiples of the smallest angle?
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find if this always happens.
Are the angles always multiples of the smallest angle?
<bookmark mark='three'/>Step one, look at one hundred twenty, two hundred forty and three hundred sixty.
They are one, two and three times one hundred twenty.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Next, look at ninety, one hundred eighty, two hundred seventy and three hundred sixty.
They are one, two, three and four times ninety.

beats.on_screen: turn by the smallest angle: the figure fits; turn by it again: the figure fits again; total turn = 2 x smallest angle, then 3 x, 4 x ...

marks.one: the figure turns by the smallest angle and a tick appears
marks.again: the figure turns by the same angle again and the total 2 x smallest angle is written
marks.more: the totals 3 x, 4 x and so on are written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step two, turn the figure by its smallest angle, and it fits.
<bookmark mark='again'/>Turn by the same angle again, and it fits again.
The total turn is two times the smallest angle.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Keep going, and the totals are three times, four times, and so on.

marks.try: a figure with smallest angle 72° appears

narration: <bookmark mark='try'/>Step three, try a figure with smallest angle seventy two degrees.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Keep adding seventy two.
The totals are seventy two, one hundred forty four, and two hundred sixteen.
Then two hundred eighty eight, and three hundred sixty.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Yes, the angles of symmetry are always multiples of the smallest angle of symmetry
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Yes, the angles of symmetry are always multiples of the smallest angle.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the lists
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble from Keeko says a figure may fit in between; a figure with smallest angle 90° is shown fitting at 100°; turned back by 90° it would fit at 10°; the bubble is struck out

marks.try: a figure with smallest angle 90° is shown fitting at 100°
marks.back: turned back by 90° the figure would fit at 10°

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks a figure may fit at an angle in between.
<bookmark mark='try'/>Say the smallest angle is ninety degrees, and the figure also fits at one hundred degrees.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Turn it back by ninety degrees, and it would fit after only ten degrees.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Ten is smaller than the smallest angle, which cannot be, so no angle fits in between.
